film.title: The Green Coat
film.logline: In November 1956 a young woman takes a coat off a hook in Budapest and walks out of Hungary; seventy years later the same coat hangs in a kitchen full of people who exist because she did.

global_style.style: 1956 archival feel, 16mm film grain, halation blooming on the highlights, slight gate weave, shallow depth of field, desaturated muted grade, 16:9
global_style.palette: wet slate grey, dirty snow white, lamp amber, marsh brown, cold moon blue
global_style.avoid: text, subtitles, captions, watermarks, logos, interface elements, distorted hands, extra limbs, fast cuts, camera shake, handheld jitter, modern clothing, modern cars, plastic, mobile phones, faces in close-up, swastikas, Nazi imagery, World War Two uniforms, weapons aimed at people, blood, gore, saturated red

shots.title: The hook
shots.job: Establish. Introduce the anchor object and the warm room she is about to leave.
shots.prompt: A woman's hands lift a heavy dark green wool overcoat off an iron hook on the back of an apartment door in Budapest in November 1956. The coat has a hand-stitched grey repair on the left cuff. She holds the coat still for a moment before pulling it down off the hook. Her face is never in frame.
shots.camera: static locked-off medium, 50mm, framed square on the door with the hook at chest height, no camera movement
shots.lighting: single warm table lamp behind camera, no fill, the top corners of the door falling into deep shadow
shots.audio: a clock ticking in the next room, faint street noise muffled through glass, one unaccompanied violin note held underneath, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: other people in frame, packed suitcases piled up, wartime propaganda posters

shots.title: The street after
shots.job: Escalate. Say why she is leaving without showing violence.
shots.prompt: An empty Budapest boulevard at first light seen from the middle of the road. A tram stands stopped and abandoned on its rails with both doors open. Shattered shop glass lies across the wet cobblestones and loose paper leaflets drift slowly along the gutter. There are no people anywhere in the frame.
shots.camera: static locked-off extreme wide, 28mm, one-point perspective straight down the tram rails, horizon locked, no camera movement
shots.lighting: flat grey overcast dawn, no visible sun, low contrast everywhere except the black interior of the tram
shots.audio: wind, loose paper scraping over stone, a distant unattended tram bell, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: crowds, soldiers, tanks, fire, explosions, rubble piles, bodies

shots.title: Looking back at the city
shots.job: The first of the two rhyming framings. She leaves.
shots.prompt: A woman in a dark green wool overcoat with a hand-stitched grey left cuff stands under a streetlamp at the edge of an empty Budapest square, seen from directly behind, and slowly turns her head to look back down the street she came from. She is in silhouette and her face is not visible at any point.
shots.camera: static locked-off wide from directly behind her at her shoulder height, 50mm, the figure small in the lower third of the frame, no camera movement
shots.lighting: one overhead streetlamp directly above her throwing a hard pool of amber light, everything beyond the pool completely black
shots.audio: her boots on wet stone, then silence, one low sustained cello note, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: other pedestrians, car headlights, her face turning fully to camera

shots.title: Night walking
shots.job: Time passing, and the anchor takes damage.
shots.prompt: The hem of a dark green wool overcoat and a pair of worn leather boots walking through frozen mud in the dark, a small cardboard suitcase swinging at knee height beside them. Mud is caked up the coat to the knee. Nothing above the waist is visible and nothing beyond a couple of metres is visible.
shots.camera: steady low tracking shot at ankle height moving backwards ahead of her at walking pace, 35mm, shallow depth of field
shots.lighting: one weak handheld torch beam entering from off-frame and raking across the mud, everything past two metres in total darkness
shots.audio: boots pulling out of thick mud, steady breathing, wind in dry grass, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: faces, other walkers, road surfaces, streetlights

shots.title: The marsh
shots.job: Peak. She is one small thing in a country-sized landscape.
shots.prompt: An extreme wide of a flat frozen border marsh under an enormous night sky, reeds standing taller than a person, and one tiny distant figure in a dark overcoat wading through shallow water far away in the middle of the frame. Two faint torch beams sweep along the horizon behind her.
shots.camera: static locked-off extreme wide, 24mm, horizon locked in the lower quarter of the frame, no camera movement
shots.lighting: cold moonlight from high camera left, the distant figure backlit and completely black, mist glowing where the moonlight passes through it
shots.audio: water moving around legs, reeds knocking together, a dog barking a long way off, a low sub-bass drone, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: soldiers, dogs in frame, gunfire, searchlight towers, fences with barbed wire in close-up, boats

shots.title: The turn
shots.job: The turn. Shot 3's framing repeated exactly, one country later.
shots.prompt: A woman in a dark green wool overcoat with a hand-stitched grey left cuff stands still in shallow marsh water, seen from directly behind, and slowly turns her head to look back the way she came. Her breath is visible in the cold. Her face is not visible at any point. She is the only thing in the frame that is not landscape.
shots.camera: static locked-off wide from directly behind her at her shoulder height, 50mm, the figure small in the lower third of the frame, no camera movement
shots.lighting: cold moonlight from high camera left, a hard rim of light on one shoulder only, everything ahead of her black
shots.audio: wind in reeds, one long breath, an unaccompanied violin note held a beat too long, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: her face turning fully to camera, other figures, torchlight hitting her

shots.title: The door
shots.job: Arrival. Two light sources meeting at a threshold.
shots.prompt: A farmhouse door in rural Austria swings inward at grey dawn and warm interior light falls across a pair of mud-caked leather boots and the frozen hem of a dark green wool overcoat standing on the step outside. A stranger's hand comes into the light holding out an enamel mug. No faces are visible.
shots.camera: static locked-off low medium, 40mm, framed on the doorstep from inside the house looking out, no camera movement
shots.lighting: warm interior lamplight spilling from behind camera onto the step, cold blue dawn beyond the door, the two colours meeting exactly at the threshold
shots.audio: a door hinge, wind cutting off as the door opens, a kettle somewhere inside, the violin resolving onto a second note, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: faces, welcome signs, flags, uniformed officials, paperwork

shots.title: The same hook, seventy years later
shots.job: Pay off. Shot 1's framing repeated, in colour, now.
shots.prompt: The same dark green wool overcoat with a hand-stitched grey repair on the left cuff hangs on an iron hook on the back of a door in a warm modern family kitchen. Beyond it and out of focus a long table is being laid for a party and someone walks past carrying a cake. No faces are visible. Style: clean modern digital capture, no film grain, natural colour, shallow depth of field, 16:9. Palette: warm daylight white, oak brown, and one deep saturated red on the party table.
shots.camera: static locked-off medium, 50mm, framed square on the door with the hook at chest height exactly as in the first shot, one slow focus rack from the coat to the room behind it
shots.lighting: bright soft daylight through a large window camera right, warm and even, no hard shadow anywhere on the coat
shots.style_note_for_humans: shot 8 deliberately leaves the 1956 look behind; its style and palette are written into the prompt above because skip_global drops the shared block
shots.audio: indistinct warm room tone of many people talking with no intelligible words, cutlery on plates, the violin joined by a second violin, no dialogue
shots.extra_avoid: film grain, sepia, vintage look, text, banners with lettering, numerals, balloons or candles spelling a number, party hats, faces

notes.assumed_clip_length: Written to hold 8 seconds of content each. Sora's clip options run longer than that depending on your plan; generate at the longest length available and trim in the edit rather than letting the model invent a second event to fill the time.
notes.consistency_anchor: The dark green wool overcoat with a hand-stitched grey repair on the left cuff. It appears in every single shot and its state is the film's clock: clean on a hook (1), on her back (3), mud to the knee (4), soaked and frozen (6), steaming in a doorway (7), clean on a hook again (8).
notes.second_anchor_the_light: The light travels warm lamp -> grey overcast -> single streetlamp -> one torch beam -> moonlight -> warm and cold meeting at a threshold -> full daylight. If a regenerated shot fights the sequence, it is the wrong take.
notes.rhyming_framings: Shots 3 and 6 share a camera line word for word, and shots 1 and 8 share a camera line word for word. Do not paraphrase either pair. That repetition is the whole structure.
notes.palette_break: Shot 8 deliberately drops the shared 1956 style and palette: modern digital, full colour, and the first saturated red in the film on the party table. This is intentional. Do not 'fix' shot 8 to match the others.
notes.no_faces_rule: The film is shot entirely from behind, beside, and below its subject. No clear face in any shot. This is a style, and it is also the only reliable way to stop the model inventing eight different women.
notes.settings_to_hold_fixed: Same aspect ratio, same model, same resolution, same seed if Sora exposes one, on all eight generations. Change nothing between shots except the prompt.
